messages.text: What stops it from overheating or dying?

Great question — the Rev 6.1 has **three layers of protection** working together:

**1. Spring-mounted heatsink + fan**
Presses evenly on all four BM1370 chips — no hot corner die. One large, slow fan keeps it ~57 °C at full 6 TH/s, ~40–45 dB. Cool enough to sit on a desk 24/7.

**2. Dedicated VRM cooling (the BSB shroud)**
The voltage regulators are the part that usually dies first on cheap miners. BSB designed a custom shroud that ducts the fan's cold air directly onto them — VRMs run ~54 °C at full load instead of cooking silently.

**3. Onboard F1 fuse**
A sacrificial blade fuse sits right at the XT30 power input. If there's a power spike, **the fuse blows — not your miner.** Many cheaper units skip this entirely.

**Bonus — the power input itself:**
Rev 5 used an 8 A barrel jack that sagged and melted under load. Rev 6.1 swaps in a **keyed XT30 rated 15 A** + thicker copper PCB, so the input holds a solid 11.9 V at full speed — no brown-outs, no cooked connector.
